author: Alice
text: @alice-codex propose a deterministic dash for this tiny game: move is 10 units, dash should be 30. Ask @bob-codex to settle what happens to a coin at position 100 when a dash crosses it. Keep the discussion to one short paragraph each; no implementation yet.

author: Alice's Codex
text: Make each move a fixed 10-unit step and each dash a fixed 30-unit step in the chosen direction, triggered once per press so holding the key can’t repeat it. @bob-codex, should a dash from 80 to 110 collect the coin at 100? I favor checking the whole traveled segment, including the endpoint, so crossing and landing on a coin both collect it exactly once.

author: Bob's Codex
text: @alice-codex I’d collect the coin at 100 whenever the 30-unit dash crosses or lands on it, once only. Check the full movement segment in either direction: 80→110, 70→100, and 120→90 collect; 60→90 misses. Coin collection shouldn’t shorten the dash.

author: Bob
text: @alice-codex before we build: what is the smallest coinScore API change to handle a dash crossing 100? Propose the signature, then ask the other Codex to check the edge cases and confirm.

author: Alice's Codex
text: Propose `coinScore(position, previousPosition = position)`: keep the destination argument and add an optional start position, awarding the coin when 100 lies within the inclusive interval between them. Existing one-argument calls retain landing-only behavior; the collected state still prevents repeat awards. @bob-codex, please check forward and reverse crossings, landing exactly at 100, starting at 100, misses, and already-collected coins, then confirm.

author: Bob's Codex
text: @alice-codex Confirmed: `coinScore(position, previousPosition = position)` covers both directions. With an uncollected coin, `(110, 80)`, `(90, 120)`, `(100, 70)`, and `(130, 100)` award it; `(90, 60)` misses. One-argument `(100)` awards, `(110)` misses. Starting at 100 includes the coin, even with no movement; already-collected coins award nothing in every case, enforced by the existing collected-state guard.

author: Bob
text: @bob-codex correction from the actual project: the existing API is coinScore(position, alreadyCollected). Preserve those arguments and add previousPosition as an optional THIRD argument. Please settle that correction with Alice’s Codex before we split the work.

author: Bob's Codex
text: @alice-codex Correction: use `coinScore(position, alreadyCollected, previousPosition = position)`, preserving both existing arguments. Return no award when `alreadyCollected` is true; otherwise check whether 100 lies in the inclusive start-to-destination interval. `(110, false, 80)` and `(90, false, 120)` collect; `(110, true, 80)` does not. Existing two-argument calls keep landing-only behavior. Please confirm this corrected signature before we split the work.

author: Alice's Codex
text: @bob-codex Confirmed: `coinScore(position, alreadyCollected, previousPosition = position)` supersedes my earlier proposal and preserves existing calls. Movement should capture the position before the step and pass it as the third argument after moving; collection checks both endpoints and never shortens the 30-unit dash.

author: Alice
text: @bob-codex while both tasks are running, give us a compact playtest sequence for verifying the corrected crossing rule once the contributions are integrated.

author: Bob's Codex
text:
Alice, use a fresh reset for each case:

- Move eight times to 80, dash to 110: collect once and finish at 110.
- Move seven times to 70, dash to 100: collect once on landing.
- Move six times to 60, dash to 90: no coin; move to 100: collect once.
- After collecting, cross 100 again: score stays unchanged.
- With test state set to 120 and the coin uncollected, dash back to 90: collect once. Starting at 100 uncollected and dashing to 130 should also collect once.

The last two setups need controlled state because traveling past 100 normally already collects the coin.
